# Trip Plan: NFL Matchday Weekend — New Orleans
**Anchor match: Atlanta Falcons @ New Orleans Saints — Monday, October 5, 2026, 7:15 PM CT (8:15 PM ET), *Monday Night Football* on ESPN**
Caesars Superdome, 1500 Sugar Bowl Drive, New Orleans, LA 70112 (NFL Week 4)

*Verified on NFL.com's official Week 4 schedule. This is exactly 30 days from today (Sep 5, 2026). Bonus: NFL flex-scheduling only applies to Weeks 12–17, so this kickoff time is locked and won't move.*

## Suggested shape: Sat Oct 3 → Tue Oct 6 (3 nights)
A Monday-night game means flying in over the weekend, so the "explore" days come *before* the match rather than after.

| Day | Plan |
|---|---|
| **Sat Oct 3** | Arrive, settle into CBD/Warehouse District, evening in the French Quarter |
| **Sun Oct 4** | National WWII Museum + Ogden Museum; watch early NFL games at a local bar |
| **Mon Oct 5** | Sazerac House late morning → early dinner → **kickoff 7:15 PM** |
| **Tue Oct 6** | Beignets, Magazine Street stroll, afternoon flight home |

## Getting there and to the stadium
**Airport → downtown** (MSY, ~14 miles):
- **Taxi** — flat rate **$36** for 1–2 passengers to the CBD/French Quarter; **$15 per person** for 3+. ~20–25 min. Best for fixed, predictable pricing.
- **Rideshare** — ~$36 minimum, but surge pricing applies. Same journey time.
- **RTA 202 Airport Express bus** — ~$1.25–1.50, but 45–60 min. Cheap-but-slow option.

**Hotel → Superdome:** Stay in the **CBD or Warehouse District** and you can simply walk — the Superdome sits on the edge of downtown, roughly 15–20 minutes on foot from the French Quarter. The **Loyola Avenue and Canal Street streetcar lines** both stop within a couple of blocks. Driving is the weakest option: garage parking around the Dome sells out and post-game exit traffic is slow. **Walk or streetcar, and skip the car entirely.**

## Eating: Cochon Butcher (pre-game pick)
930 Tchoupitoulas St — a ~15-minute walk from the Superdome, in the Warehouse District.

This is the deliberate choice for *this specific* match. A big caveat about New Orleans: **many of the city's best restaurants close on Mondays**, which is a real trap for a Monday-night game. I checked hours specifically — Cochon Butcher is **open Mondays 11 AM–10 PM**, takes **no reservations**, and serves fast enough that you can eat at 5:00–5:30 and stroll to the Dome comfortably before a 7:15 kickoff. Excellent Cajun-style sandwiches and boudin.

Backups nearby: Herbsaint, Compère Lapin, Mother's (classic po'boys), Manning's (sports bar, walkable). **Confirm Monday hours before you go** — this is the single most likely thing to trip up the plan.

## Exploring the area
All within walking distance of the venue:
- **National WWII Museum** (945 Magazine St) — the city's top-rated attraction, ~15 min walk. Open **daily 9 AM–5 PM**, adults from **$37**. Budget 3–4 hours; a good Sunday anchor.
- **Sazerac House** (101 Magazine St) — cocktail history museum/distillery, ~12 min walk, free admission.
- **Ogden Museum of Southern Art** (925 Camp St) — next to the WWII Museum.
- **Champions Square** — the plaza right outside the stadium; the pre-game gathering spot, worth arriving early for.
- **French Quarter, Canal Street & Magazine Street** — a few blocks further for nightlife, architecture and shopping.

## Practical notes
- **Clear bag policy is enforced.** Only a clear bag up to 12"×6"×12", or a 1-gallon clear ziplock, plus a small clutch (~4.5"×6.5"). **No backpacks.** Buy a clear bag before you travel.
- **Tickets:** SeatGeek is the Saints' official primary ticketing partner; Ticketmaster carries verified resale. Entry is **mobile-only**, so install the Saints or SeatGeek app and load tickets in advance. *(As instructed, I have not purchased anything.)*
- **Weather:** early-October highs 80–83°F, lows 59–62°F, still humid. Light breathable clothing, comfortable shoes for uneven Quarter sidewalks, a light layer for evening, and a compact rain jacket. The Superdome is a domed, air-conditioned venue, so the match itself is weather-proof.

## Before you book
Two things worth re-checking closer to the date: restaurant Monday hours, and museum admission prices (these were current at the time of research). Everything else — the fixture, venue, and transport options — is locked in.

I made no bookings or purchases at any point; this is research only, ready for you to act on.
